highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 strengthens platform support and fixes reliability issues across native, Android, Linux, and browser workloads.
highlights_body: Apple deployment requirements are updated, WebGPU browser packaging is simplified, and several managed and native paths now avoid crashes, leaks, and unnecessary allocations.

breaking.title: Apple deployment minimums increased
breaking.body: Native SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp assets now require macOS 11 or later and iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst 14 or later. Update affected application deployment targets before upgrading.

bullets.detail: Native Apple assets now use consistent macOS 11 and iOS, tvOS, and Mac Catalyst 14 baselines, with managed platform metadata aligned to the native requirements.
Packages the required emdawnwebgpu C++ support in the native WebAssembly archive, so consumer application links no longer compile that source with their own C or C++ settings.
Updates the Windows build toolchain, ANGLE, Windows App SDK, and WebView2 integration used by WinUI, MAUI, and Uno packages.

bullets.lead: SKData string creation is safer and more efficient
bullets.detail: SKData.FromCString now avoids reading past its native buffer and writes directly into SKData; managed image pixel copies also avoid an intermediate allocation when direct raster copying is valid.
Bundled HarfBuzz functions bind locally, preventing incompatible system HarfBuzz symbols loaded by GTK from being used with bundled objects.
Android texture views pace continuous rendering to the display refresh rate, and front-buffered managed streams no longer retain their source unnecessarily.
HarfBuzzSharp reuses UTF-32 encoding buffers and avoids native feature-string allocations while preserving existing decoding behavior.
